scope_text: Bounded synthetic profile only. The comparator applications (the OPA application and the LangGraph plus OPA application) are configured by Cognous, not vendor implementations. This is not independent certification and not production readiness; operational trust stays on HOLD. Linux only.
status: Declarations of the protected-destination column for the Wiki subset (amendment 76; PR-1 and section 7 of the pre-registration; rule of the draft amendment 79). Generated by comparators/runner/declare_ocs_column.py from the executable scenarios of the plan file and from sentences that were published before it. No scenario of any set has been run on any configuration; no result, expected status or behaviour of a configuration was read to make a declaration.

plan.note: A declaration is valid for a scenario while its scenario_sha256 equals the digest of the scenario in the plan file. A plan file that gains or changes scenarios needs the declarations to be generated again and reviewed.

rules: R1. A step is applied to the destination exactly when its declared interface can express it (ocs_column.classify_step). A scenario with a step that cannot be expressed is declared NOT-EXPRESSIBLE, citing the interface item that lacks the field, operation or state and the sentence of the case that the scenario was written from.

R2. Expressible steps: execute through the eight request fields to the one target that a destination grant pins; a clock step; the zero-argument controls revoke, fence, rotate, reopen and break_audit; revoke_grant:<grant> for a grant of the declared world. Every other control, and every call to another target, has no counterpart.

R3. A scenario whose steps are all expressible but whose question is carried in issuer_claims or in payload content (which the destination records and never reads) is declared NOT-CLAIMED only when a sentence published before the plan states what OCS does not claim for the case (a not-claimed sentence of the applicability file at its pinned revision, or amendment 39); it is still run and its observation is retained apart from the scored results (amendment 74). Without such a sentence the declaration would be void and the scenario is ASKED.
R4. Any other scenario is ASKED and scored by the same oracle as the comparator applications.
R5. A declaration does not depend on the expected statuses of the scenario and is made before any result exists.
world_mapping: Every grant of the declared Wiki world is provisioned at the destination the way the registered fixture provisions its own grant: policy "policy1", target "sink", principal "agent", the lifetime (expires_at) and the effect count (max_effects) of the world's grant record, one fence generation. A destination grant pins one target, so a call to any other target is outside every grant (rule R2). The 16 grants that are provisioned in addition to the registered one use 16 of the 128 admission attempts of the first interval of 60 clock units (interface item DEST-INGRESS); the largest executable scenario of the plan file makes 101 calls.

DEST-EXEC-ARGS.description: The execute operation takes exactly eight argument fields: grant, effect, generation, policy, target, payload, verifier_status, issuer_claims. Any other field is refused.
DEST-EXEC-ARGS.marker: exact(a,'grant effect generation policy target payload verifier_status issuer_claims')

DEST-GRANT-FIELDS.description: A grant record has exactly these fields: id, scope, generation, principal, policy, target, credential_version, dependency_version, modes, max_effects, expires_at. There is no field for an agent, a user, a set of tools, an approval, a window, a parent or a budget level other than max_effects.
DEST-GRANT-FIELDS.marker: exact(a,'id scope generation principal policy target credential_version dependency_version modes max_effects expires_at')

DEST-TARGET-PIN.description: A grant pins exactly one target and one policy; a request whose target or policy differs from the grant is refused by the hard pin.

DEST-OPERATIONS.description: The destination accepts a closed list of operations: fence, destination_grants, provision, revoke, execute, ingress_recover. There is no operation for stopping an agent, recording a delegation, an exception, an approval or a tool, or for changing a policy engine.

DEST-REVOKE.description: The revoke operation takes one field, grant, and closes that grant.

DEST-CLAIMS-DIGEST.description: issuer_claims is carried and bound into the request, but the destination only records its digest in the resolution input; no decision reads a claim.

DEST-PAYLOAD-OPAQUE.description: payload is bound by the request digest and stored as canonical text; the destination does not read inside it.

DEST-BUDGET.description: One budget level per grant: max_effects counts the effects of that grant.

DEST-EXPIRY.description: A grant expires at expires_at, read from the host clock; the expiry instant is outside the grant.

DEST-CLOCK.description: The destination reads a host clock that the harness sets; a scenario clock step sets it.

DEST-INGRESS.description: A fixed admission budget of 128 attempts per interval of 60 clock units applies to every command, including the commands that provision grants.

DEST-REOPEN.description: The registered adapter reopens the destination from the persisted file.

DEST-CONTROLS.description: The registered adapter offers the zero-argument controls revoke (the default grant), fence, rotate, reopen and break_audit.

DEST-FAULTS.description: The registered request builder offers the faults missing_verifier, stale_verifier, forged_signature and wrong_actor.
